stem: Between which two consecutive measurements did the antibody level increase the most?
stimulus: The line graph shows one patient's antibody level, measured every 7 days after a vaccination.

figure.caption: Antibody Level After Vaccination
figure.alt: A line graph with five points joined in order: day 0 at 10, day 7 at 60, day 14 at 90, day 21 at 70, and day 28 at 20 units per mL.

explanation: For each segment, take the later value minus the earlier one. Day 0 to day 7 goes from 10 to 60, an increase of 50. Day 7 to day 14 goes from 60 to 90, an increase of 30. The other two segments go down. The largest increase is day 0 to day 7. This is the core of the SAT question that asks 'during which interval did the value increase the most': you compare how far each segment rises, not how high its points sit.

B.why: This segment ends at the highest point on the graph, but it rises only 30 (from 60 to 90). You compared where the segments end instead of how much each one changed.

C.why: This segment starts at the peak, so it stands out on the graph, but the level falls from 90 to 70. The question asks about the change over each interval, not about where the peak is.

D.why: This is the steepest segment, but it falls from 70 to 20, a decrease of 50. The question asks for an increase, so a decrease doesn't count, however large it is.

stem: In which year was the number of working looms the lowest?
stimulus: The line graph shows the number of working looms in one weaving mill, counted every 10 years.

figure.caption: Working Looms in a Weaving Mill
figure.alt: A line graph with five points joined in order: 1820 at 40, 1830 at 25, 1840 at 55, 1850 at 70, and 1860 at 35 looms.

explanation: Find the point that sits lowest on the vertical axis. That point is at 25 looms, and it lines up with 1830. Every SAT line-graph question that asks for the highest or lowest point uses this single read: find the height, then read the time below it.

A.why: 1820 is the first year shown, not the lowest point. Its value is 40, which is above the 25 in 1830. You assumed the graph starts at its minimum instead of checking each height.

C.why: 1850 has 70 looms, the highest point on the graph. The question asks for the lowest point, so you picked the opposite extreme.

D.why: 1860 ends the biggest drop on the graph (70 down to 35), but 35 is still above 25. You picked where the largest decrease ends instead of where the value is lowest.

stem: In which week did the studio pull exactly 120 prints?
stimulus: The line graph shows the number of prints a printmaking studio pulled each week over 5 weeks.

figure.caption: Prints Pulled per Week
figure.alt: A line graph with five points joined in order: week 1 at 80, week 2 at 140, week 3 at 120, week 4 at 160, and week 5 at 100 prints.

explanation: Find 120 on the vertical axis, move across to the point at that height, and read the week below it. That point is week 3. This unlocks the SAT line-graph question that names a value and asks when it happened: start on the vertical axis, not the horizontal one.

A.why: Week 2 sits one gridline higher, at 140. You read the gridline above 120 instead of the 120 line itself.

C.why: Week 4 is the highest point, at 160. The question asks for a specific value, not the maximum, so you picked the extreme instead of reading the stated height.

D.why: Week 5 sits one gridline lower, at 100. You read the gridline below 120 instead of the 120 line itself.

stem: Between which two consecutive samples did the percentage of fern spores decrease the most?
stimulus: The line graph shows the percentage of fern spores among all fossil spores and pollen found in rock samples. A sample was taken for every 2,000 years after the start of the record.

figure.caption: Fern Spores in Fossil Samples
figure.x_label: Thousands of years after start of record
figure.alt: A line graph with five points joined in order: 0 at 20 percent, 2 at 35 percent, 4 at 30 percent, 6 at 10 percent, and 8 at 15 percent.

explanation: Find the drop across each segment. From 2 to 4 the value falls from 35 to 30, a decrease of 5. From 4 to 6 it falls from 30 to 10, a decrease of 20. The other two segments rise. The largest decrease is from 4 to 6. This is the SAT question that asks 'during which interval was the decrease greatest': the steepest downward segment wins.

A.why: This segment rises from 20 to 35, the biggest increase on the graph. The question asks for a decrease, so you answered with the opposite direction.

B.why: This segment starts at the highest point, 35, but it falls only 5, to 30. You chose where the line starts high instead of measuring how far each segment drops.

D.why: This segment starts at the lowest point, 10, so it sits lowest on the graph. But it rises to 15. You looked for low values instead of the largest drop across an interval.
